earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 q32026earningsreleaseex991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 NEWS RELEASE www.northerntrust.com INVESTOR CONTACT: Stephen Carroll | 312-557-3474 | Stephen.Carroll@ntrs.com MEDIA CONTACT: John O'Connell | 312-444-2388 | John.O'Connell@ntrs.com NORTHERN TRUST CORPORATION REPORTS THIRD QUARTER NET INCOME OF $642.9 MILLION, EARNINGS PER DILUTED COMMON SHARE OF $3.40 CHICAGO , OCTOBER 21, 2026 — Northern Trust Corporation today reported third quarter net income per diluted common share of $3.40, compared to $4.23 in the second quarter of 2026 and $2.29 in the third quarter of 2025. Net income was $642.9 million, compared to $792.2 million in the prior quarter and $457.6 million in the prior-year quarter. Third Quarter 2026 results included the following notable items: • $48.7 million (pre-tax) impact to Other Noninterest Income from notable items (after-tax $36.8 million): • $34.0 million (pre-tax) gain on the sale of the guardianship services business, recognized in Other Operating Income (after-tax $25.7 million). • $14.7 million (pre-tax) incremental gain related to Northern Trust’s participation in the second Visa Exchange Offer, recognized in Other Operating Income (after-tax $11.1 million). MICHAEL O’GRADY, CHAIRMAN AND CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER: “Northern Trust delivered strong third-quarter results, demonstrating continued progress against our One Northern Trust strategy. Compared to the prior year and excluding notable items, revenues grew 11%, while disciplined expense management generated more than 600 basis points of positive operating leverage. As a result, pretax income increased 21% and earnings per share increased 40%. All three businesses delivered organic trust-fee growth, reflecting strong execution across the company. Market conditions continued to evolve but remained constructive overall. Our diversified business model positions us to perform across a range of environments. Our strong capital position enabled us to return more than $1.5 billion to common shareholders year to date. As we enter the final quarter of the year, we remain focused on supporting our clients, investing in growth and delivering sustainable long-term value to shareholders.” FINANCIAL SUMMARY & KEY METRICS % Change Q3 2026 vs. ($ In Millions except per share data) Q3 2026 Q2 2026 (1)(2) Q3 2025 Q2 2026 Q3 2025 Trust, Investment and Other Servicing Fees $ 1,373.0 $ 1,349.5 $ 1,265.5 2 % 8 % Other Noninterest Income 250.0 673.0 169.1 (63) 48 Net Interest Income (FTE*) 679.1 683.1 596.3 (1) 14 Total Revenue (FTE*) $ 2,302.1 $ 2,705.6 $ 2,030.9 (15) % 13 % Noninterest Expense $ 1,492.5 $ 1,638.6 $ 1,422.9 (9) % 5 % Provision for Credit Losses 5.4 (5.3) (17.0) N/M N/M Provision for Income Taxes 153.6 272.5 161.9 (44) (5) FTE Adjustment* 7.7 7.6 5.5 1 41 Net Income $ 642.9 $ 792.2 $ 457.6 (19) % 40 % Earnings Allocated to Common Shares $ 621.9 $ 782.2 $ 437.2 (20) % 42 % Diluted Earnings per Common Share $ 3.40 $ 4.23 $ 2.29 (20) 48 Return on Average Common Equity 20.1 % 25.9 % 14.8 % Average Assets $ 159,235.9 $ 163,575.8 $ 151,041.5 (3) % 5 % (1) For Q2 2026, Other Noninterest Income included a $525.4 million gain related to Northern Trust's participation in the second Visa Exchange Offer and a $73.9 million loss on available for sale debt securities sold in conjunction with a repositioning of the portfolio. reference.summary: Northern Trust Corporation, a financial holding company, provides wealth management, asset servicing, asset management, and banking solutions for corporations, institutions, families, and individuals. It operates in two segments, Asset Servicing and Wealth Management. The Asset Servicing segment offers asset servicing and related services, including custody, fund administration, investment operations outsourcing, investment management, investment risk and analytics services, employee benefit services, securities lending, foreign exchange, treasury management, brokerage, transition management, banking, and cash management services. It serves corporate and public retirement funds, foundations, endowments, fund managers, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, and other institutional investors.
